lines.text: A buyer says the package never came.
You have days to prove it, or lose the sale.
Meet Priya. She runs a two-person ceramics shop.
Every dispute is a guess: fight it, offer something, or just refund and lose the money.
Dispute Defender reads the case from PayPal and tells her which.
Her disputes, in one place: money at risk, and the deadline that matters most.
And the agent's call on all seven cases: defend two, a fair offer on one, refund three, hold one.
One click. The agent reads the dispute, the order and the tracking from PayPal, ties every claim to a record, and gives its verdict: defend.
And if a draft ever cites a record that doesn't exist, our server strikes it out.
Claude drafts the reply. Tap any claim to see the record behind it.
Before anything is sent, she sees exactly what PayPal will receive, evidence pack included.
She approves. This is PayPal's live sandbox: these responses come straight from PayPal's Disputes API.
In the sandbox, we trigger PayPal's decision. PayPal's API records the case as won: resolved in the seller's favour.
A second case: two mugs arrived chipped, so a fair offer is smarter. The buyer wrote in Spanish, so the message to her is in Spanish too.
And when the evidence says the buyer is right, it says refund. No tricks.
Plates shipped without tracking? It won't pretend. She can't prove delivery, so it says refund.
It lists every action PayPal allows right now, picks one, and says why not the others.
No more guessing.
It even spots patterns, so the next dispute never starts.
Single cases teach too: ask for the unit number at checkout.
Any AI assistant gets the same judgement through MCP, and you can try it without keys.
Under the hood: PayPal's APIs and Agent Toolkit gather the facts, Claude writes, our server checks every claim, and you decide.
Dispute Defender. Win the disputes worth fighting. Settle the rest fairly.
